label: Design discipline
summary: A design discipline is a named, recognised field of practice with its own skills, methods, and professional identity. Conversation design is an instance of a design discipline, meaning it qualifies as a real profession rather than just a loose set of tasks. Maaike uses this framing to argue that conversation design deserves to be taken seriously as a distinct field of work.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike positions conversation design as a legitimate design discipline to push back against the idea that anyone can just build a bot without specialist knowledge. She points out that many companies do not yet know the profession has a name, which means job seekers have to search under related terms and build visibility through informal networks. The discipline framing also lets her argue that good conversation design saves organisations rework, grounding the professional claim in practical value.
open_questions: At what point does a set of skills become recognised enough to be called a discipline, and is conversation design there yet?
How does conversation design relate to adjacent disciplines like UX writing or content design, and where do the boundaries sit?
